fixed_features.feature: One highlighted cell, one-based row then column
fixed_features.justification: The lesson explicitly defines first subscript as row and second as column.

fixed_features.feature: Five radio options or source-shaped blank fields
fixed_features.justification: Preserves observed response contracts; five options do not justify a fixed relative correct-choice role.

shortcut_probes.cue: Visible normalized coordinate arrangement in the answer bank: q-13498
shortcut_probes.strategy: Infer relative correct coordinate from the choice-set shape alone; ambiguous shape predicts minimum row/minimum column. Never inspect the highlighted matrix.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline is random selection among five choices. Perfect q-13498 prediction is structurally forced by fixed offsets; the ambiguous shape has conflicting roles and is not a perfect predictor. Small q-13503/q-13499 samples are supporting observations, not broad statistical estimates.

shortcut_probes.subgroup: exact delivered batch, matching radio item
shortcut_probes.strategy: Choose middle column among the three choices having the smallest row index.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: The batch has one such item (seed 3782988955); the same forced rule succeeds in 28/28 independent examples. Baseline is one of five choices. This is a generator construction defect present in the batch, not a claim that one rule answers every batch item.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Select first option without reading it.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: No perfect position cue demonstrated; comparison is random one-of-five selection. Actual UI can reorder choices, while the demonstrated bank-shape cue survives any order.

delivery.result: No records removed: 5/5 batch and 120/120 fresh samples survive at captured basis 5667. Selection does not rebalance answer-bank roles; any surviving matching item retains its shortcut. No stored generated record defect demonstrated.

limitations: No live database, future inventory, policy weights or learner history examined. Read-only selection analysis cannot determine actual learner draw frequencies.
